title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Trial of Civil Cases by Summary Procedure

articles.content_en:
Article 2 For civil cases tried by a Primary People's Court under the ordinary procedure of first instance, where all parties voluntarily choose to apply the summary procedure and the People's Court approves upon examination, the summary procedure may be applied for adjudication.
The People's Court shall not convert the ordinary procedure into the summary procedure in violation of the principle of voluntariness of the parties.

Article 3 Where a party raises an objection to the application of the summary procedure and the People's Court considers the objection to be established, or where the People's Court discovers during adjudication that it is inappropriate to apply the summary procedure, the case shall be transferred to the ordinary procedure for adjudication.
II. Prosecution and Defense

Article 4 Where the plaintiff personally cannot write the statement of prosecution, and indeed has difficulty in entrusting another person to write it on his or her behalf, the plaintiff may prosecute orally.
Where the plaintiff prosecutes orally, the People's Court shall accurately record the basic information, contact information, litigation claims, facts and reasons of the party, and shall register the relevant evidence. The People's Court shall read the contents of the aforesaid records and registrations aloud to the plaintiff in person, and the plaintiff shall sign or affix a fingerprint after confirming that they are correct.

Article 5 A party shall, at the time of prosecution or defense, provide the People's Court with his or her accurate service address, recipient, telephone number and other contact methods, and shall sign or affix a fingerprint for confirmation.
The service address shall clearly state the postal code and detailed address of the place of domicile of the person to be served; where the person to be served is a natural person with a fixed occupation, his or her place of employment may be deemed the service address.

Article 6 After the plaintiff prosecutes, the People's Court may, through simple means such as sending a verbal message, telephone, facsimile, or e-mail, summon both parties and witnesses at any time.

Article 7 After both parties appear in court, if the defendant agrees to an oral defense, the People's Court may hold a hearing immediately; if the defendant requests a written defense, the People's Court shall notify all parties of the time limit for submitting the statement of defense and the specific date of the hearing, and shall explain to the parties the legal consequences of adducing evidence beyond the time limit and failing to appear in court without cause. Each party shall sign or affix a fingerprint on the record and on the service receipt of the hearing summons.

Article 9 Where the defendant refuses to provide his or her service address and contact information after appearing in court, the People's Court shall inform him or her of the consequences of refusing to provide the service address; if the defendant still refuses after being informed by the People's Court, the matter shall be handled in the following manner:
(1) if the defendant is a natural person, the domicile in his or her household registration or his or her habitual residence shall be the service address;
(2) if the defendant is a legal person or an unincorporated organization, the domicile registered or recorded with the registration authority shall be the service address.
The People's Court shall record the contents of the aforesaid notification in the record.

Article 10 Where litigation documents fail to be actually received by a party because the service address provided by the party himself or herself is inaccurate, the service address is changed without timely notice to the People's Court, or the party refuses to provide his or her service address, the matter shall be handled in the following manner:
(1) if service is by mail, the date of return noted on the mail receipt shall be deemed the date of service;
(2) if service is direct, the date on which the server notes the circumstances on the service receipt on the spot shall be deemed the date of service.
The People's Court shall notify the parties of the aforesaid contents in writing or orally at the time of prosecution by the plaintiff and defense by the defendant.

Article 11 Where the natural person to be served and his or her adult family members residing together refuse to sign for litigation documents, or the person responsible for receiving mail of a legal person or unincorporated organization refuses to sign for litigation documents, the server shall, pursuant to Article 86 of the Civil Procedure Law, invite a representative of the relevant grassroots organization or the unit where the person to be served works to be present as a witness. If the invited person is unwilling to be present as a witness, the server shall record on the service receipt the reason for refusal, the time and place, and the circumstances that the invited person is unwilling to be present as a witness, and leave the litigation documents at the domicile or place of employment of the person to be served, which shall be deemed service.
Where the adult family member of the person to be served residing together or the person responsible for receiving mail of a legal person or unincorporated organization is the other party in the same case, the preceding paragraph shall not apply.
III. Preparation before Adjudication

Article 12 In civil cases tried under the summary procedure, a party and his or her litigation agent who apply for a witness to appear in court to testify shall make the application before the expiration of the time limit for adducing evidence.

Article 13 After one or both parties raise an objection to the application of the summary procedure, the People's Court shall examine the objection and handle it separately according to the following circumstances:
(1) if the objection is established, the case shall be transferred to the ordinary procedure for adjudication, and the composition of the collegiate bench and related matters shall be notified to both parties in writing;
(2) if the objection is not established, both parties shall be notified orally, and the aforesaid contents shall be recorded in the record.
The time limit for adjudication of a civil case transferred to the ordinary procedure for adjudication shall begin to be calculated from the day following the date of filing of the case by the People's Court.

Article 15 After a mediation agreement is reached and examined by the judicial personnel, if both parties agree that the mediation agreement shall take effect upon signature or affixing of fingerprints by both parties, the mediation agreement shall have legal effect from the date of signature or affixing of fingerprints by both parties. Where a party requests to excerpt or reproduce the mediation agreement, the request shall be permitted.
Where the mediation agreement complies with the preceding paragraph and does not fall under the circumstances where a mediation document need not be made, the People's Court shall separately make a civil mediation document. If one party refuses to perform after the mediation agreement takes effect, the other party may apply for compulsory execution by presenting the civil mediation document.

Article 16 The People's Court may notify the parties in court of the specific date for collecting the civil mediation document at the People's Court, or may send the civil mediation document to the parties within ten days from the day following the date on which the parties reach the mediation agreement.

Article 17 Where a party raises an objection on the ground that the civil mediation document is inconsistent with the original intent of the mediation agreement, and the People's Court, after examination, considers the objection to be established, it shall, pursuant to the mediation agreement, rule to make corrections to the relevant contents of the civil mediation document.
IV. Hearing

Article 18 Where a hearing notice sent by means such as a verbal message, telephone, facsimile, or e-mail has not been confirmed by the party or there is no other evidence sufficient to prove that the party has received it, the People's Court shall not use it as a basis for treating the case as withdrawn or for judgment by default.

Article 19 Where the parties have already been notified of their litigation rights and obligations in writing or orally before the hearing, or all parties have entrusted lawyers to act as agents in the litigation, the judicial personnel may, in addition to notifying the parties of the right to apply for withdrawal, no longer notify the parties of other litigation rights and obligations.

Article 20 For parties who have not entrusted lawyers to act as agents in the litigation, the judicial personnel shall provide necessary explanations or clarifications on withdrawal, admission, burden of adducing evidence, and other related contents, and shall, during the hearing, appropriately remind the parties to properly exercise their litigation rights and perform their litigation obligations, and guide the parties in conducting normal litigation activities.

Article 21 At the hearing, the judicial personnel may, based on the litigation claims and defense opinions of the parties, summarize the disputed issues. After confirmation by the parties, the parties shall adduce evidence, cross-examine, and debate around the disputed issues.
Where the parties have no dispute over the facts of the case, the judicial personnel may directly render a judgment or ruling after hearing the parties' debate opinions on the application of law.

Article 22 Where both parties simultaneously come to a Primary People's Court to request resolution of a simple civil dispute, but have not consulted on a time limit for adducing evidence, or the defendant has been summoned to appear in court by a simple means, and a party requests to adduce evidence in court at the hearing, the request shall be permitted; where a party has difficulty in adducing evidence in court, the time limit for adducing evidence shall be decided by the parties through consultation, but shall not exceed fifteen days at the maximum; if consultation fails, it shall be decided by the People's Court.
Article 23 Civil cases tried under the summary procedure shall be concluded at one hearing, except where the People's Court deems it truly necessary to hold another hearing.

Article 25 At the end of the hearing, the judicial personnel may, based on the adjudication of the case, give a brief summary of the disputed issues and the parties' adduction of evidence, cross-examination, and debate, and consult the parties on whether they agree to mediation.

Article 26 Where the judicial personnel discover during the adjudication that the case is complex and needs to be transferred to the ordinary procedure, they shall make a timely decision before the expiration of the adjudication time limit, and notify the parties in writing.
V. Pronouncement of Judgment and Service
Article 27 Civil cases tried under the summary procedure shall have judgment pronounced in court, except where the People's Court considers that it is inappropriate to pronounce judgment in court.

Article 28 For cases where judgment is pronounced in court, except where a party requests service by mail in court, the People's Court shall notify the parties or their litigation agents of the time limit and place for collecting the judgment document, as well as the legal consequences of failing to collect it within the time limit. The aforesaid circumstances shall be recorded in the record.
Where the People's Court has notified the parties of the time limit and place for collecting the judgment document, the date on which the party collects the judgment document within the specified time limit shall be the date of service; where the party fails to collect it within the specified time limit, the date on which the specified time limit for collecting the judgment document expires shall be the date of service, and the appeal period of the party shall begin to be calculated from the day following the date on which the specified time limit for collecting the judgment document expires.

Article 29 Where a party requests service of the judgment document by mail due to inconvenient transportation or other reasons, the People's Court may serve it by mail pursuant to the service address provided by the party himself or herself.
Where the People's Court serves by mail pursuant to the service address provided by the party himself or herself, the date of receipt or return noted on the mail receipt shall be the date of service, and the appeal period of the party shall begin to be calculated from the day following the date of receipt or return noted on the mail receipt.

Article 30 Where the plaintiff, after being summoned by summons, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons or withdraws from the courtroom midway without the permission of the court, the case may be treated as withdrawn; where the defendant, after being summoned by summons, refuses to appear in court without justifiable reasons or withdraws from the courtroom midway without the permission of the court, the People's Court may render judgment by default based on the plaintiff's litigation claims and the evidentiary materials already submitted to the court by both parties.
Where the case is treated as withdrawn or judgment by default is rendered, the People's Court may serve the judgment document upon the party who did not appear in court pursuant to the service address provided by the party himself or herself.

Article 31 For cases where judgment is pronounced on a scheduled date, the date of scheduled pronouncement shall be the date of service, and the appeal period of the parties shall begin to be calculated from the day following the scheduled pronouncement. Where a party fails to appear in court on the scheduled pronouncement date without justifiable reasons, the calculation of the appeal period for the judgment or ruling shall not be affected.
Where a party genuinely has justifiable reasons for being unable to appear in court and has already informed the People's Court before the scheduled pronouncement, the People's Court may serve the judgment document upon the party who did not appear in court pursuant to the service address provided by the party himself or herself.
Article 33 Where the judicial interpretations already published by this Court are inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.

Article 34 These Provisions shall come into force as of December 1, 2003. Civil cases accepted after December 1, 2003 shall be governed by these Provisions.
